title: 三姝媚·过都城旧居有感
title_en: San Shu Mei: Passing My Old Home in the Capital
author: 吴文英

form.en: ci to the tune San Shu Mei, in two stanzas

text_note.zh: 资料库原文“渍春衫”误作“溃春衫”，这里依通行本改正；“歌沉”原文作“歌沈”，“沈”是“沉”的古写。
text_note.en: The source text has a wrong character for zì (to stain) in the second line; this follows the common text. It also writes chén (to sink) in an old form.

readings.en: This character means to soil or stain, and is read wò.

readings.zh: “紫曲”的“曲”指街巷，读 qū，不读歌曲的 qǔ。
readings.en: In zǐ qū the character means a lane, so it is read qū, not qǔ as in 'song'.

readings.zh: “傍”是靠近、挨着的意思，读 bàng。
readings.en: This character means 'next to', and is read bàng.

glosses.zh: 湖山：湖光山色，这里指杭州西湖一带。
glosses.en: hú shān: lakes and hills, here the West Lake area in Hangzhou.

glosses.zh: 经醉惯：常常在这里喝醉，已经习惯了。
glosses.en: jīng zuì guàn: used to getting drunk here, it happened so often.

glosses.zh: 渍：沾染。
glosses.en: zì: to stain.

glosses.zh: 啼痕：泪痕。
glosses.en: tí hén: tear stains.

glosses.zh: 客长安：在京城作客。长安本是汉唐的都城，这里借指南宋都城临安，就是今天的杭州。
glosses.en: kè cháng ān: staying as a guest in Chang'an. Chang'an was the old Han and Tang capital; here it stands for Lin'an, the Southern Song capital, today's Hangzhou.

glosses.zh: 断襟零袂：破了的衣襟，碎了的袖子，形容衣衫破旧。袂，袖子。
glosses.en: duàn jīn líng mèi: torn fronts and ragged sleeves, meaning shabby clothes. Mèi means a sleeve.

glosses.zh: 涴尘谁浣：沾满灰尘，谁来替我洗呢？暗指从前替他洗衣的人已经不在了。浣，洗。
glosses.en: wò chén shuí huàn: covered in dust, who will wash them? It hints that the one who once washed his clothes is gone. Huàn means to wash.

glosses.zh: 紫曲：歌女们居住的街巷。
glosses.en: zǐ qū: the lanes where singing girls lived.

glosses.zh: 败井：废弃的井。
glosses.en: bài jǐng: an abandoned well.

glosses.zh: 青蔓：青色的藤蔓。
glosses.en: qīng màn: green creeping vines.

glosses.zh: 对语：面对面说话，这里指燕子呢喃。
glosses.en: duì yǔ: talking face to face, here the twittering of swallows.

glosses.zh: 曾巢：曾经筑过巢。
glosses.en: céng cháo: once built a nest.

glosses.zh: 谢堂双燕：化用唐代刘禹锡《乌衣巷》“旧时王谢堂前燕”。王、谢是东晋的两大豪门。燕子还是那对燕子，主人却变了。
glosses.en: xiè táng shuāng yàn: the pair of swallows from the Xie family hall, after Liu Yuxi's line about 'the swallows that once nested in the halls of the Wang and Xie families', two great clans of the Eastern Jin. The swallows are the same, but the people have changed.

glosses.zh: 须断：终究要断。
glosses.en: xū duàn: is bound to end.

glosses.zh: 怪得：奇怪的是，怎么会。
glosses.en: guài dé: strangely, how could it be that.

glosses.zh: 梦缘：像梦一样美好的缘分。
glosses.en: mèng yuán: a bond as sweet as a dream.

glosses.zh: 绣屋：装饰华美的房间。
glosses.en: xiù wū: a beautifully decorated room.

glosses.zh: 秦筝：一种弦乐器，相传出自秦地，所以叫秦筝。
glosses.en: qín zhēng: a stringed instrument, said to come from the old land of Qin.

glosses.zh: 偏爱：特别喜爱。
glosses.en: piān ài: to love especially.

glosses.zh: 舞歇歌沉：舞停了，歌声也消失了。
glosses.en: wǔ xiē gē chén: the dancing stopped and the singing died away.

glosses.zh: 红颜：年轻女子美丽的容颜，代指心爱的女子。
glosses.en: hóng yán: a young woman's lovely face, meaning the woman he loved.

glosses.zh: 先变：先变了，指人已不在。
glosses.en: xiān biàn: changed first, meaning she is gone.

glosses.zh: 伫久：站了很久。伫，久立。
glosses.en: zhù jiǔ: standing a long time.

translation.zh: 西湖的山水间，我早已醉惯了，
translation.en: Among the lakes and hills I grew used to being drunk.

translation.zh: 春衫上沾满了泪痕和酒痕，数也数不清。
translation.en: My spring robe is stained with tears and wine beyond counting.
Now I am a guest in the capital again,

translation.zh: 可叹衣襟破了、袖子碎了，
translation.en: and sigh at my torn front and ragged sleeves:
covered in dust, who will wash them now?

translation.zh: 歌女住的街巷，门前一片荒凉，
translation.en: In the lane where she lived, the gate is overgrown;

translation.zh: 顺着那口废井，风吹动青青的藤蔓。
translation.en: along the old abandoned well, the wind stirs green vines.

translation.zh: 在东边邻居家呢喃说话的，
translation.en: Twittering at the house next door

translation.zh: 还是从前在这里筑巢的，
translation.en: are the very ones that once nested here,
the pair of swallows from the Xie family hall.
Spring dreams in this world must always end,

translation.zh: 只是奇怪，当年那段梦一样的缘分怎么那么短。
translation.en: but how strange that our dream of a bond back then was so short.
In the embroidered room there was a zither.
She loved to sit by the crab-apple blossoms,
and set out a feast deep into the night.
The dancing stopped, the singing died away.

translation.zh: 海棠花还没有减少，美人却先不在了。
translation.en: The flowers have not faded, yet her lovely face has changed first.

translation.zh: 我在河桥边站了很久，想走，
translation.en: I stand a long time by the river bridge, wanting to leave,
and in the setting sun my eyes are full of tears.

background.zh: 题目意思是：经过都城里的旧居，有所感触。这里的都城是南宋的临安，就是今天的杭州。吴文英年轻时在杭州住过，和一位女子相爱，一说她是歌女，后来去世了。多年后他再经过从前的住处，门巷荒凉，燕子依旧，人却不在了，于是写下这首词。写作年份不清楚。
background.en: The title means: feelings on passing my old home in the capital. The capital was Lin'an, the Southern Song capital, today's Hangzhou. When young, Wu Wenying lived in Hangzhou and loved a woman there; some say she was a singing girl. She later died. Years afterwards he passed his old home again. The lane was overgrown, the swallows were the same, but she was gone, so he wrote this ci. We do not know the year.

author_note.zh: 吴文英（约1200—约1260），字君特，号梦窗，南宋词人。他一生没有做大官，多在苏州、杭州一带给官员做幕僚。他的词用字华丽，想象跳跃，读起来像一幅幅交错的画面。他写了很多怀念旧日恋人的词，这首就是其中一首。
author_note.en: Wu Wenying (about 1200 – about 1260) was a Southern Song ci poet. He never held high office and spent most of his life as an adviser to officials around Suzhou and Hangzhou. His ci use rich words and leap from image to image, like overlapping pictures. He wrote many ci in memory of a lost love, and this is one of them.

appreciation.zh: 这首词从一件旧衣服写起：春衫上又是泪痕又是酒痕，衣服破了，没人来洗。一个“谁”字，就透露出那个替他洗衣的人已经不在了。再看旧居：门巷荒凉，废井边藤蔓摇动，只有那对燕子还在，好像什么都没变。下阕回到从前：她在海棠花边弹筝，深夜摆宴，热闹又温暖。可“舞歇歌沉”，一切都停了，海棠还开着，人却先没了。最后他站在桥边，想走又走不开，夕阳照着满脸的泪。花在人亡，物是人非，悲伤一层层加深。
appreciation.en: The poem begins with an old robe. It is stained with tears and wine, torn, and no one washes it. The single word 'who' tells us the person who used to wash it is gone. Then we see the old home. The lane is overgrown, vines sway by the abandoned well, and only the pair of swallows is still there, as if nothing had changed. The second stanza goes back in time. She played the zither by the crab-apple blossoms and set out feasts late at night, lively and warm. But the dancing and singing stopped. The blossoms still bloom, yet she is gone first. At the end he stands by the bridge, wanting to leave but unable to, tears on his face in the setting sun. The flowers remain while the person is gone: the places are the same, the people are not, and the grief grows layer by layer.
